claim: Kinetochores are multi-subunit protein assemblies that link chromosomes to microtubules of the mitotic and meiotic spindle.
source: Kinetochores are multi-subunit protein assemblies that link chromosomes to microtubules of the mitotic and meiotic spindle.
evidence: This is a foundational statement about kinetochore function that represents established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Cdk1 phosphorylation activates phospho-degrons on the essential subunit Ame1CENP-U.
source: we demonstrate that Cdk1 phosphorylation activates phospho-degrons on the essential subunit Ame1CENP-U, which are recognized by the E3 ubiquitin ligase complex SCF-Cdc4.
evidence: This claim is supported by multiple experimental approaches including phosphorylation mapping, in vitro kinase assays, and molecular dynamics simulations presented in the manuscript.

claim: Phospho-degrons on Ame1 are recognized by the E3 ubiquitin ligase complex SCF-Cdc4.
source: we demonstrate that Cdk1 phosphorylation activates phospho-degrons on the essential subunit Ame1CENP-U, which are recognized by the E3 ubiquitin ligase complex SCF-Cdc4.
evidence: This is demonstrated through experiments showing Ame1 accumulation in SCF mutants and molecular dynamics simulations of peptide-Cdc4 binding.

claim: Gradual phosphorylation of degron motifs culminates in M-phase and targets the protein for degradation.
source: Gradual phosphorylation of degron motifs culminates in M-phase and targets the protein for degradation.
evidence: This is supported by cell cycle analysis showing stepwise phosphorylation of Ame1 with maximal phosphorylation in M-phase followed by disappearance of phosphorylated forms.

claim: Binding of the Mtw1Mis12 complex shields the proximal phospho-degron, protecting kinetochore-bound Ame1 from the degradation machinery.
source: Binding of the Mtw1Mis12 complex shields the proximal phospho-degron, protecting kinetochore-bound Ame1 from the degradation machinery.
evidence: This is demonstrated by in vitro kinase assays showing reduced Ame1 phosphorylation when bound to Mtw1c, and anchor-away experiments showing increased phosphorylation when Mtw1 is removed.

claim: Artificially increasing degron strength partially suppresses the temperature sensitivity of a cdc4 mutant.
source: Artificially increasing degron strength partially suppresses the temperature sensitivity of a cdc4 mutant, while overexpression of Ame1-Okp1 is toxic in SCF mutants, demonstrating the physiological importance of this mechanism.
evidence: This is shown through serial dilution assays demonstrating that Ame1-CPDILTPP partially rescues growth defects of cdc4-1 mutants.

claim: Overexpression of Ame1-Okp1 is toxic in SCF mutants.
source: Artificially increasing degron strength partially suppresses the temperature sensitivity of a cdc4 mutant, while overexpression of Ame1-Okp1 is toxic in SCF mutants, demonstrating the physiological importance of this mechanism.
evidence: This is demonstrated by serial dilution assays showing growth defects when Ame1-Okp1 is overexpressed in skp1-3 and cdc34-2 mutant backgrounds.

claim: Budding yeast kinetochores consist of more than 40 different proteins.
source: This is remarkable as even the relatively simple kinetochores in budding yeast consist of more than 40 different proteins.
evidence: This represents established knowledge about the composition of budding yeast kinetochores.

claim: The inner kinetochore comprises 16 subunits, which are collectively called the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN, or Ctf19CCAN in budding yeast).
source: The inner kinetochore comprises 16 subunits, which are collectively called the constitutive centromere-associated network (CCAN, or Ctf19CCAN in budding yeast).
evidence: This is established knowledge about kinetochore organization cited from previous work.

claim: Kinetochore assembly upon replication of centromere DNA occurs rapidly and is completed within 10–15 min.
source: Live cell imaging experiments suggest that kinetochore assembly upon replication of centromere DNA occurs rapidly and is completed within 10–15 min (Tanaka et al., 2007).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous live cell imaging work.

claim: Ame1 and Okp1 are essential for cell viability in budding yeast.
source: the COMA complex, which consists of the conserved subunits Ctf19CENP-P, Okp1CENP-Q, Mcm21CENP-O, and Ame1CENP-U, of which Ame1 and Okp1 are essential for cell viability in budding yeast (Hornung et al., 2014).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work establishing essentiality.

claim: The CCAN directly binds to a specialized nucleosome by recognizing the histone H3 variant Cse4CENP-A via the Mif2 and Ame1-Okp1 subunits.
source: The CCAN directly binds to a specialized nucleosome by recognizing the histone H3 variant Cse4CENP-A via the Mif2 and Ame1-Okp1 subunits (Anedchenko et al., 2019; Fischböck-Halwachs et al., 2019; Killinger et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citations to recent structural and biochemical studies.

claim: High levels of Cse4CENP-A lead to its mis-incorporation into non-centromeric loci.
source: High levels of Cse4CENP-A lead to its mis-incorporation into non-centromeric loci (Heun et al., 2006; Ranjitkar et al., 2010; Van Hooser et al., 2001)
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies demonstrating mis-incorporation.

claim: In budding yeast, Cse4CENP-A protein levels are controlled via regulated proteolysis involving the E3 ubiquitin ligase Psh1.
source: In budding yeast, Cse4CENP-A protein levels are controlled via regulated proteolysis involving the E3 ubiquitin ligase Psh1, which prevents mis-incorporation of Cse4 into chromosome arms (Ranjitkar et al., 2010).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work on Cse4 regulation.

claim: The Mub1/Ubr2 E3 ligase complex regulates the level of the Dsn1 subunit.
source: Additional links between the ubiquitin-proteosome system and kinetochore assembly in budding yeast are provided by the Mub1/Ubr2 E3 ligase complex, which regulates the level of the Dsn1 subunit (Akiyoshi et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: More than 70 phosphorylation sites on nine different CCAN subunits were detected by mass spectrometry analysis of native yeast CCAN subunits.
source: In total, this analysis detected more than 70 phosphorylation sites on nine different CCAN subunits (Table 1, Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: This is directly supported by the mass spectrometry data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Nine phosphorylation sites followed the minimal consensus motif for Cdk1 phosphorylation (S/TP).
source: Of these sites, nine followed the minimal consensus motif for Cdk1 phosphorylation (S/TP), while four sites (in the subunits Mcm21CENP-O, Nkp1, and Cnn1CENP-T) followed the full Cdk1 consensus (S/TP_K/R).
evidence: This is based on analysis of the phosphorylation sites detected by mass spectrometry.

claim: Ame1 has a cluster of four minimal Cdk1 sites being phosphorylated in the N-terminus of the protein.
source: our analysis identified Ame1 as a candidate Cdk1 target, with a cluster of four minimal Cdk1 sites being phosphorylated in the N-terminus of the protein.
evidence: This is based on mass spectrometry analysis of native Ame1.

claim: Ame1 displayed a noticeable shift in migration in SDS-PAGE upon phosphorylation with Cdc28-Clb2.
source: Ame1 displayed a noticeable shift in migration in SDS-PAGE upon phosphorylation with Cdc28-Clb2, but less so with Cdc28-Clb5 (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is directly observed in the in vitro kinase assay shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Clb2-Cdk1 preferentially phosphorylated Ame1, whereas Clb5-Cdk1 preferred Okp1 in the Ame1-Okp1 complex.
source: Quantitative phosphorylation analysis confirmed that in the Ame1-Okp1 complex Clb2-Cdk1 preferentially phosphorylated Ame1, whereas Clb5-Cdk1 preferred Okp1.
evidence: This is based on quantitative analysis of in vitro kinase assays.

claim: The phosphorylation of the Ame1-Okp1 complex was dependent on the hydrophobic patch in Clb5 and Clb2 cyclins.
source: The phosphorylation of the Ame1-Okp1 complex was dependent on the hydrophobic patch, a known substrate docking region in Clb5 and Clb2 cyclins, and a slightly stronger docking potentiation was seen in case of Okp1 (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is demonstrated by comparing phosphorylation with wild-type and hydrophobic patch mutant cyclins.

claim: Mapped phosphorylation sites on Ame1 in vitro closely corresponded to the sites detected on native Ame1.
source: The mapped phosphorylation sites closely corresponded to the sites detected on native Ame1, in particular phosphorylation of the residues Thr31, Ser41, Ser45, and Ser52/Ser53 was both detected in vivo and in vitro (Figure 1C).
evidence: This is based on comparison of mass spectrometry data from native and in vitro phosphorylated Ame1.

claim: Conservation of Ame1 phospho-sites can be detected in the most closely related Saccharomyces species.
source: Conservation of these phospho-sites can be detected in the most closely related Saccharomyces species (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is shown through multiple sequence alignment analysis.

claim: Wild-type Ame1 displayed multiple slowly migrating forms that were eliminated in the 7A mutant.
source: Analysis of log phase extracts showed that wild-type Ame1 displayed multiple slowly migrating forms that were eliminated in the 7A mutant (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is directly observed in western blot analysis.

claim: Ame1-7E migrated much more slowly than wild-type in SDS-PAGE.
source: By contrast, Ame1-7E migrated much more slowly than wild-type, its position in SDS-PAGE corresponding to the most slowly migrating forms of Ame1-WT.
evidence: This is observed in western blot analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Ame1-7A and -7E mutants were viable when expressed as the sole source of Ame1 in the cell.
source: Ame1-7A and -7E mutants were viable when expressed as the sole source of Ame1 in the cell.
evidence: This is demonstrated through genetic complementation experiments.

claim: Both Ame1-7A and -7E variants supported viability with little difference in growth rate on rich media compared to wild-type Ame1.
source: In an anchor-away approach, in which endogenous Ame1 is removed from the nucleus upon addition of rapamycin, both Ame1-7A and -7E variants supported viability with little difference in growth rate on rich media compared to wild-type Ame1 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is shown through serial dilution assays in the anchor-away system.

claim: Deleting the region harboring the entire phospho-cluster (Δ31–116) yielded a slow growth phenotype.
source: Analysis of internal truncations, which maintained the essential Mtw1c-binding N-terminus (residues 1–15), showed that deleting the region harboring the entire phospho-cluster (Δ31–116) yielded a slow growth phenotype, while a more extensive deletion was inviable (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is demonstrated through serial dilution assays of truncation mutants.

claim: The non-phosphorylatable Ame1-7A mutant accumulated to much higher protein levels compared to wild-type after 5 hr in galactose.
source: Strikingly, the non-phosphorylatable Ame1-7A mutant accumulated to much higher protein levels in the same time span, leading to a roughly fourfold increase in steady-state level compared to wild-type after 5 hr in galactose (Figure 2B, C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through western blot analysis and quantification of overexpression experiments.

claim: Okp1 expressed from the same plasmid showed no change in protein level in the different Ame1 mutants.
source: By contrast, Okp1 expressed from the same plasmid showed no change in protein level in the different Ame1 mutants, arguing that differences in plasmid stability or mitotic retention cannot be the cause for the observed effect on the Ame1 protein level.
evidence: This is observed in western blot analysis and serves as an internal control.

claim: Preventing phosphorylation at Ser41, Ser45, or Ser52/53 led to accumulation of Ame1 protein.
source: Analysis of Ame1 protein levels after 5 hr of expression in the presence of galactose showed that preventing phosphorylation on Thr31 had relatively little effect on Ame1 level when compared to the wild-type. By contrast, preventing phosphorylation at Ser41, Ser45, or Ser52/53 led to accumulation of the protein, roughly similar to preventing phosphorylation altogether in the 7A mutant (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through western blot analysis of individual phospho-site mutants.

claim: The Ame1 sequence surrounding Ser52 and Ser53 (motif 1) showed similarity to a cyclin E-type phospho-degron.
source: the Ame1 sequence surrounding Ser52 and Ser53 (motif 1) showed similarity to a cyclin E-type phospho-degron, comprehensively described in the context of the Cdk1 inhibitor Sic1 (Kõivomägi et al., 2011; Nash et al., 2001)
evidence: This is based on sequence comparison with known phospho-degron motifs and supported by citations.

claim: The combination of Ser41/Ser45 (motif 2) resembled a di-phospho-degron with a typical +4 spacing between phosphorylated residues.
source: while the combination of Ser41/Ser45 (motif 2) resembled a di-phospho-degron with a typical +4 spacing between phosphorylated residues found for example in the acetyltransferase Eco1 (Hao et al., 2007; Lyons et al., 2013; Lyons and Morgan, 2011; Figure 2G).
evidence: This is based on sequence analysis and comparison with known di-phospho-degrons, supported by citations.

claim: The doubly phosphorylated Ser41/Ser45 peptide is predicted to be a good Cdc4 binder based on molecular dynamics simulations.
source: The analysis of the trajectories allowed us to predict that the doubly phosphorylated Ser41/Ser45 peptide should be a good Cdc4 binder.
evidence: This is based on computational molecular dynamics simulations showing stable binding interactions.

claim: Phospho-Ser41 establishes hydrogen bond interactions with the guanidino groups of Arg485 and Arg534 of Cdc4.
source: Phospho-Ser41 establishes hydrogen bond interactions with the guanidino groups of Arg485 and Arg534 of Cdc4 while phospho-Ser45 of the peptide establishes hydrogen bond interactions with Arg467 of Cdc4 (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is predicted from molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: The doubly phosphorylated peptide showed a strong hydrogen bond network at the binding pocket of Cdc4.
source: Overall, the doubly phosphorylated peptide showed a strong hydrogen bond network at the binding pocket of Cdc4, highlighting the potential of this peptide as a Cdc4 binder.
evidence: This is based on analysis of molecular dynamics simulation trajectories.

claim: The doubly phosphorylated Ser41/Ser45 peptide establishes more interactions with Cdc4 with respect to the singly phosphorylated variants.
source: The simulations also indicated that the doubly phosphorylated Ser41/Ser45 peptide establish more interactions with Cdc4 with respect to the singly phosphorylated variants (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Videos 1–3).
evidence: This is demonstrated through comparative molecular dynamics simulations.

claim: Ame1-WT expressed from the GAL promoter strongly accumulated in the skp1-3 mutant relative to a wild-type background.
source: Western blotting showed that Ame1-WT expressed from the GAL promoter strongly accumulated in the skp1-3 mutant relative to a wild-type background (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is directly observed in western blot analysis.

claim: The phospho-forms of Ame1 were preserved in the skp1-3 mutant.
source: The phospho-forms of Ame1 were preserved under these conditions, showing that the skp1-3 mutant uncouples phosphorylation of Ame1 from its degradation.
evidence: This is observed in western blot analysis and demonstrates that SCF is required for degradation but not phosphorylation.

claim: Okp1 accumulated in the skp1-3 mutant background.
source: Interestingly, under these conditions, also an accumulation of Okp1, expressed from the same plasmid, was apparent.
evidence: This is observed in western blot analysis.

claim: Overexpressed Ame1 accumulated in mutant alleles of Cdc53CUL1, Cdc34, and Cdc4.
source: Similar to the skp1-3 mutant, overexpressed Ame1 accumulated in mutant alleles of the Cullin subunit Cdc53CUL1, the E2 enzyme Cdc34, and the F-box protein Cdc4.
evidence: This is demonstrated through western blot analysis in multiple SCF mutant backgrounds.

claim: Ame1 levels remained low in a deletion mutant of the F-box protein Grr1.
source: By contrast, Ame1 levels remained low (or were even decreased relative to wild-type) in a deletion mutant of the cytoplasmic F-box protein Grr1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is observed in western blot analysis and indicates specificity for Cdc4.

claim: Okp1 strongly accumulated (30-fold increase) in the cdc4-1 mutant.
source: Interestingly, the SCF mutants also had a pronounced effect on the level of overexpressed Okp1, with particularly strong accumulation (30-fold increase) observable in the cdc4-1 mutant.
evidence: This is quantified from western blot analysis.

claim: Overexpression of AO compromised growth in skp1-3 mutant background at 30 and 34°C.
source: In a skp1-3 mutant background, however, overexpression of AO, either in wild-type form or with Cdk1 sites mutated to alanine, compromised growth at 30 and 34°C (Figure 4C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through serial dilution assays.

claim: Overexpression of the full four-protein COMA complex was toxic in wild-type strain background.
source: While overexpression of Ame1-Okp1 or Ctf19-Mcm21 (CM) subcomplexes was tolerated in a wild-type strain background, overexpression of the full four-protein COMA complex was toxic, indicating that maintenance of the proper protein level of this complex is critical for viability (Figure 4D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through serial dilution assays.

claim: The VQPILTPPKL peptide (Ame1-CPDILTPP) is predicted to be a potent Cdc4 binder based on molecular dynamics simulations.
source: Overall, this strong network of peptide-protein interactions indicates that the VQPILTPPKL peptide is predicted to be a potent Cdc4 binder, even more than the doubly phosphorylated Ser41/Ser45 peptide.
evidence: This is based on molecular dynamics simulations showing extensive interactions.

claim: Neither Ame1 nor Okp1 protein was detectable by western blotting upon overexpression of Ame1-CPDILTPP.
source: Strikingly, neither Ame1 nor Okp1 protein was detectable by western blotting upon overexpression under these conditions, and preventing phosphorylation on the five remaining sites (Ame1-5A-CPDILTPP) did not stabilize the protein (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is directly observed in western blot analysis.

claim: The Ame1-CPDILTPP mutant and Okp1 were detectable and displayed similar levels as the wild-type proteins in a cdc4-1 background.
source: Combining the Ame1-CPDILTPP allele with the cdc4-1 mutant demonstrated that this is indeed the case: the Ame1-CPDILTPP mutant and also Okp1 were detectable and displayed similar levels as the wild-type proteins in a cdc4-1 background (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is demonstrated through western blot analysis and confirms Cdc4-dependent degradation.

claim: Ame1-CPDILTPP expressed as the sole copy of Ame1 yielded a viable strain with slight temperature sensitivity at 37°C and increased sensitivity to benomyl.
source: Interestingly, Ame1-CPDILTPP expressed as the sole copy of Ame1 yielded a viable strain, which showed slight temperature sensitivity at 37°C and increased sensitivity to benomyl (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is demonstrated through serial dilution assays.

claim: Ame1-CPDILTPP was able to partially suppress the growth defect of cdc4-1 at 34°C and improved growth in the presence of hydroxyurea and benomyl.
source: Upon combination with a cdc4-1 mutant, however, Ame1-CPDILTPP was able to partially suppress the growth defect of cdc4-1 at 34°C and improved growth in the presence of hydroxyurea and benomyl.
evidence: This is demonstrated through serial dilution assays and indicates physiological relevance of the degron.

claim: Motif 1/2 phosphorylation of endogenous Ame1 was cell cycle dependent.
source: Western blotting showed that motif 1/2 phosphorylation of endogenous Ame1 was cell cycle dependent (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is demonstrated through western blot analysis of cells arrested at different cell cycle stages.

claim: S-phase-arrested cells displayed a single slowly migrating Ame1 form in addition to unmodified Ame1, while M-phase-arrested cells were maximally phosphorylated with two slowly migrating forms.
source: S-phase-arrested cells displayed a single slowly migrating Ame1 form in addition to unmodified Ame1, while M-phase-arrested cells were maximally phosphorylated with two slowly migrating forms becoming apparent.
evidence: This is observed in western blot analysis of cell cycle arrests.

claim: Motif 1/2 phosphorylation occurred in a stepwise manner with fully phosphorylated forms appearing 30 min into the cell cycle.
source: Consistent with the analysis of the arrests, we observed that motif 1/2 phosphorylation occurred in a stepwise manner with fully phosphorylated forms appearing 30 min into the cell cycle.
evidence: This is demonstrated through time-course western blot analysis after release from alpha-factor arrest.

claim: Phosphorylated Ame1 forms gradually diminished between minute 30 and 60 after release from alpha-factor.
source: Strikingly, phosphorylated Ame1 forms gradually diminished between minute 30 and 60 and only unmodified Ame1 and a single slowly migrating form remained (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is observed in time-course western blot analysis.

claim: Full phosphorylation of Ame1 is mutually dependent on the presence of both motif 1 and motif 2.
source: Interestingly, Ame1 mutants in which only phosphorylation on motif 1 was allowed (Ame1-5A1) or only on motif 2 (Ame1-5A2) also largely eliminated the characteristic stepwise phosphorylation of Ame1-3A (Figure 6—figure supplement 1D, E), showing that full phosphorylation is mutually dependent on the presence of both motif 1 and motif 2.
evidence: This is demonstrated through western blot analysis of single motif mutants.

claim: At the semipermissive temperature of 34°C, skp1-3 cells completed replication with nearly wild-type kinetics and accumulated phosphorylated Ame1-3A.
source: At the semipermissive temperature of 34°C, skp1-3 cells completed replication with nearly wild-type kinetics and accumulated phosphorylated Ame1-3A (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through cell cycle analysis with western blotting and FACS.

claim: In skp1-3 cells at 34°C, phosphorylated Ame1 forms persisted and the cells remained in mitosis with a 2C DNA content.
source: In contrast to wild-type cells, however, the phosphorylated Ame1 forms persisted and the cells remained in mitosis with a 2C DNA content.
evidence: This is observed in cell cycle analysis combining western blotting and FACS.

claim: Inclusion of the Mtw1 complex strongly reduced the incorporation of phosphate into Ame1 in vitro kinase assays.
source: Analysis of in vitro kinase assays revealed that while Ame1 was heavily phosphorylated in isolation, inclusion of the Mtw1 complex strongly reduced the incorporation of phosphate into Ame1 under identical conditions (Figure 7B).
evidence: This is directly demonstrated through in vitro kinase assays.

claim: Upon removal of Mtw1 from the nucleus, phosphorylation at Ame1 degron motifs 1/2 gradually increased over time.
source: We observed that upon removal of Mtw1 from the nucleus, phosphorylation at Ame1 degron motifs 1/2 gradually increased over time (Figure 7D).
evidence: This is demonstrated through anchor-away experiments with western blot analysis.

claim: Slowly migrating forms of Ame1 disappeared over time when Mtw1 was removed from the nucleus upon inhibition of protein synthesis by cycloheximide.
source: Upon inhibition of protein synthesis by cycloheximide, slowly migrating forms of Ame1 disappeared over time when Mtw1 was removed from the nucleus (Figure 7E).
evidence: This is demonstrated through anchor-away experiments combined with cycloheximide treatment.

claim: Ame1 variants lacking the N-terminal Mtw1c interaction domain display a prominent slowly migrating form when motif1/2 phosphorylation is permitted.
source: We found that Ame1 variants in which motif1/2 phosphorylation is permitted (Ame1-3A-ΔN) display a prominent slowly migrating form, which is eliminated in the Ame1-4A-ΔN mutant (Figure 7—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is observed in western blot analysis of N-terminal deletion mutants.

claim: Cdk1 phosphorylation generates phospho-degron motifs on selected inner kinetochore subunits, including the essential COMA subunit Ame1.
source: This study reveals novel aspects of phospho-regulation at the budding yeast inner kinetochore. We show that an important function of Cdk1 phosphorylation is to generate phospho-degron motifs on selected inner kinetochore subunits, including the essential COMA subunit Ame1, which are then recognized by the conserved ubiquitin ligase complex SCF with its phospho-adapter Cdc4.
evidence: This is the main conclusion synthesized from multiple experimental approaches.

claim: Ame1 and Mcm21 peptides were identified in a large-scale proteomic study as being simultaneously regulated by phosphorylation and ubiquitination.
source: We note that Ame1 and Mcm21 peptides were also identified in a large-scale proteomic study geared towards enriching peptides simultaneously regulated by phosphorylation and ubiquitination (Swaney et al., 2013).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a previous proteomic study.

claim: Ubiquitination of COMA subunits was detected for Okp1 (on residue Lys57) and Mcm21 (on residue Lys229).
source: In this context, ubiquitination of COMA subunits was detected for Okp1 (on residue Lys57) and Mcm21 (on residue Lys229).
evidence: This is cited from a previous proteomic study.

claim: Only a subset of Ame1 is phosphorylated and subjected to the SCF-dependent pathway.
source: There are, however, important aspects in which the inner kinetochore subunit Ame1 differs from previously studied SCF substrates: while, for example, the Cdk1 inhibitor Sic1 is fully degraded at the G1-S transition to allow replication initiation, our experiments indicate that only a subset of Ame1 is phosphorylated and subjected to the SCF-dependent pathway.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that Ame1 shows partial phosphorylation and cells remain viable.

claim: The pool of Ame1 regulated by SCF corresponds to molecules that are not bound to their binding partner within the kinetochore, the Mtw1c.
source: Our biochemical experiments furthermore suggest that the pool of Ame1 regulated by this mechanism corresponds to molecules that are not bound to their binding partner within the kinetochore, the Mtw1c.
evidence: This is inferred from experiments showing Mtw1c binding protects Ame1 from phosphorylation and degradation.

claim: Phospho-degrons could be ideally suited as assembly sensors for kinetochores since they allow to distinguish excess subunits from properly assembled ones.
source: In this context, phospho-degrons could be ideally suited as assembly sensors for kinetochores since they allow to distinguish excess subunits from properly assembled ones.
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the experimental findings.

claim: Cse4 has been identified as an SCF substrate in budding yeast.
source: Notably, a recent study has identified Cse4 as an SCF substrate in budding yeast and shown that Cse4 overexpression aggravates the growth defects of SCF mutants (Au et al., 2020).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: Assembly and turnover of CBF3 complexes are defective in SCF mutants.
source: Moreover, assembly and turnover of CBF3 complexes are defective in SCF mutants and both complexes contain Skp1 as a subunit (Kaplan et al., 1997).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous work.

claim: Skp1 mutants influence the levels of the Mis12 complex at human kinetochores.
source: Skp1 mutants also influence the levels of the Mis12 complex at human kinetochores (Davies and Kaplan, 2010; Gascoigne and Cheeseman, 2013), indicating that SCF-mediated regulation may be a conserved aspect of kinetochore biology.
evidence: This is supported by citations to studies in human cells.

claim: The Ame1-7A mutant effectively prevents phosphorylation in vivo and in vitro.
source: While our experiments strongly implicate Ame1 as a Cdk1 and SCF substrate, they also show that the Ame1-7A mutant effectively prevents phosphorylation in vivo and in vitro, but does not induce a strong mitotic delay such as the skp1-3 mutant.
evidence: This is demonstrated through western blot and in vitro kinase assays.

claim: Additional phospho-targets beyond Ame1 must exist to fully account for the mitotic defects of SCF mutants.
source: We speculate that the Ame1-7A mutant is not sufficient to fully prevent the mitotic defects of SCF, and additional phospho-targets must exist.
evidence: This is speculated based on the observation that Ame1-7A does not fully phenocopy SCF mutants.

claim: Human CENP-U has been established as a kinetochore receptor for Plk1.
source: Potential kinases include Cdc5/Plk1 and indeed Ame1 residues Ser52/Ser53 constitute candidate Polo-box binding sites, and human CENP-U has been established as a kinetochore receptor for Plk1 (Singh et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citation to a recent study.

claim: Cdc4, Cdc34, and Cdc53 remain essential genes in sic1Δ mutants, demonstrating that there must be additional key substrates.
source: Previous work has defined the role of SCF-Cdc4 at the G1-S transition, but has also shown that Cdc4, as well as Cdc34 or Cdc53, remain essential genes in sic1Δ mutants (Schwob et al., 1994), demonstrating that there must be additional key substrates.
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous genetic studies.

claim: SCF mutants that complete replication arrest at G2-M with a short spindle and an activated mitotic checkpoint.
source: Furthermore, SCF mutants that complete replication arrest at G2-M with a short spindle and an activated mitotic checkpoint (Goh and Surana, 1999; Schwob et al., 1994) (our unpublished observations).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous studies and unpublished observations.

claim: Ctf19CCAN subunits are cell cycle-dependent substrates of SCF-Cdc4.
source: Our experiments indicate that Ctf19CCAN subunits are cell cycle-dependent substrates of SCF-Cdc4 and open up the possibility that regulation of kinetochores by SCF makes a critical contribution to the metaphase-anaphase transition.
evidence: This is the main conclusion from the experimental data presented.

claim: Kinetochores are molecularly linked to SCF, the other major RING-type E3 ligase complex that regulates the eukaryotic cell cycle.
source: They also reveal that in addition to the well-established relationship between kinetochores and the E3 ligase APC/C, which regulates the metaphase-anaphase transition via the mitotic checkpoint complex, kinetochores are also molecularly linked to SCF, the other major RING-type E3 ligase complex that regulates the eukaryotic cell cycle.
evidence: This is a conclusion synthesized from the experimental findings.
